examName: Maharashtra Education Service, Group B (Collegiate Branch) - Lecturer in English
examPattern: Written Examination / Screening Test followed by Document Verification or Interview

topics: Dramatic Theory: The Renaissance, Elizabethan Drama, Neo-classicism, Restoration Drama, Drama of Ideas.
Dramatic Theory: Poetic Drama, Absurd Drama, Drama and Social Realism, Modern Indian Drama.
Texts: William Shakespeare - Hamlet, Ben Jonson - Volpone, William Congreve - The Way of the World, George Bernard Shaw - Arms and the Man.
Texts: T.S. Eliot - Murder in the Cathedral, Arthur Miller - Death of a Salesman, Harold Pinter - The Birthday Party, Girish Karnad - The Fire and the Rain.
Poetic Theory: Metaphysical Poetry, The Epic and the Mock-epic, The Romantic Movement, Victorian Poetry.
Poetic Theory: Modernism in Poetry, Experimental trends in Modern Poetry, Myth in Modern Poetry, Symbolism in Modern Poetry, Confessional Poetry.
Texts: John Donne - ‘Canonization’, ‘Death be not proud’, ‘Love’s War’, ‘Good Morrow’; Andrew Marvell - ‘To his Coy Mistress’, ‘Eyes and Tears’, ‘Bermudas’, ‘The Garden’.
Texts: John Milton - ‘Paradise Lost’, Book I and II; William Wordsworth - ‘She dwelt among untrodden ways’, ‘Tintern Abbey’, ‘She was a Phantom of Delight’, ‘Ode on the Intimations of Immortality’.

Texts: John Keats - ‘The Eve of Saint Agnes’, ‘La Belle Dame Sans Merci’, ‘Ode on a Grecian Urn’, ‘Ode to a Nightingale’; Robert Browning - ‘My Last Duchess’, ‘A Grammarian’s Funeral’, ‘Andrea Del Sarto’, ‘The Patriot’.
Texts: Alfred Tennyson - ‘The Lotus Eaters’, ‘Ulysses’, ‘Crossing the Bar’, ‘The Lady of Shalott’.
Texts: William Butler Yeats - ‘Byzantium’, ‘Leda and the Swan’, ‘Among School Children’, ‘A Prayer for My Daughter’; T.S. Eliot - ‘The Waste Land’.
Texts: Ted Hughes - ‘Crow’s Song of Himself’, ‘Crow on the Beach’, ‘Crow and the Birds’, ‘Crow’s Nerve Fails’; Sylvia Plath - ‘Morning Song’, ‘Spinster’, ‘The Courage of Shutting Up’, ‘Three Women’.

Texts: Nissim Ezekiel - ‘The Egoist’s Prayer’, ‘Background Casually’, ‘Night of the Scorpion’, ‘Goodbye Party to Miss Pushpa T.S.’; Kamala Das - ‘An Introduction’, ‘The Sunshine Cat’, ‘My Grandmother’s House’, ‘A Hot Noon in Malabar’.
Theory of the Novel: The Rise of the middle class, The Rise of the Reading Public, The Rise of the Novel, The Novel and the Romance, The Victorian Novel.
Theory of the Novel: The stream of consciousness Novel, Colonization and Post-Colonism, Symbolism and the Novel, Novel and Social Commitment, Feminist concerns in the Indian English Novel.
Texts: Henry Fielding - Tom Jones, Jane Austen - Sense and Sensibility, Charles Dickens - David Copperfield, Herman Melville - Moby Dick.
Texts: Joseph Conrad - The Heart of Darkness, Ernest Hemingway - The Old Man and the Sea, Mulkraj Anand - Untouchable, William Golding - Lord of the Flies, Shashi Deshpande - That Long Silence.

units.unitTitle: The Beginnings of English Studies in India & The Status of English in Independent India
topics: The impact of Colonialism on India – the culture contact and the problem of acculturation.
The Anglicist v/s Orientalist debate. Macaulay’s minute of 1835 on Indian Education. Introduction of English Language and Literature in India.
Rise of Nationalism in the English Educated Indian middle class, Imperialism and Orientalism.

Reference Books: Gauri Vishwanathan - Masks of Conquest, Rajeshwari Sundar Rajan - The Lie of the Land, Edward Said - Orientalism, Leela Gandhi - Post-Colonial Theory, Bernard Cohn - Colonialism and its forms of knowledge, Partha Chatterjee - The Nation and its Fragments.
The Language policy of the Government of India - English as Associate Official Language.
Position of English in the Three-Language Formula - English as a Second/Foreign Language in Independent India.
Uses of English in India today: As a Link Language, Library Language and Language of Business and Commerce.
English in Mass Communication - Indianisation of English Grammar and Phonology - ‘Chutnification’ of English in Indian Writing in English.

Reference Books: V.K. Gokak - English in India, Braj Kachru - Indianisation of English & The Other Tongue, Bansal and Harrison - Spoken English for India, N. Krishnaswamy and Archana S. Burde - The Politics of India’s English.
